Student Medical Assessment, Annual: Primary One And Equivalent Age Groups
Primary Five And Equivalent Age Groups
column4: Due to change in immunisation schedule, medical examination by doctor is also conducted for both Primary 5 and Primary 6 students in 2008 and discontinued for Primary 6 students from 2009.

Due to SARS outbreak in 2003, 85 Secondary schools were not covered.  Discontinued screening for Secondary 5 students and only examined Secondary 3 students with health problems with effect from 1 January 2006.  Prior to 2008, data refer to educational levels other than Primary 1 and 6 students.  In 2008, data refer to educational levels other than Primary 1, Primary 5 and Primary 6.  With effect from 2009, data refer to educational levels other than Primary 1 and Primary 5 students.  Prior to January 2016, data refer to screening by nurses for all Primary 2, 3, 4 and 6, as well as Secondary 1, 2, 4 students, and only Secondary 3 students with health problems.  With effect from January 2016, data refer to screening by nurses for all Primary 2, 3, 4 and 6, as well as Secondary 1, 2 students, and only Secondary 3 & 4 students with health problems.

Prior to 2008, data refer to general medical examination done for students excluding Primary 1 and Primary 6.  In 2008, data refer to general medical examination done for students excluding Primary 1 , Primary 5 and Primary 6.  With effect from 2009, data refers to general medical examination done by doctors for students in other educational levels.  With effect from 2019, include Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme is conducted for all Secondary 1, 4 and 5 female students.  With effect from 2020, data include Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme conducted for all Secondary 2 and 3 female students.
